integrity: Analytical proof and reproducible deterministic consistency program are included. Publication-priority assessment is qualified and external independent verification has not occurred.
scientific_limitations: A single spatially uniform two-state process modulates all wave numbers; this is not the spatially correlated Gaussian field of the motivating source.
Instability refers to exponentially growing annealed moments, while each fixed nonzero mode has strictly negative almost-sure Lyapunov exponent.
A moment instability requires the instantaneous tension to be negative for some intervals, so it does not demonstrate buckling with strictly positive instantaneous tension.
Continuous-wave-number band results must be intersected with allowed wave numbers on finite periodic domains.
No nonlinear buckling saturation, additive forcing, spatially varying tension or experimental verification is proved.

The scalar tilted-telegraph moment exponent and the distinction between almost-sure and annealed exponents were already obtained in general multiplicative-flow models; the candidate addition is the full bending-mode and periodic-size threshold optimization.
The oscillatory finite-size correction is specific to a one-dimensional periodic geometry with quantized wave numbers.
title: Moment-order buckling and oscillatory finite-size thresholds for telegraph-modulated surfaces
